text: {"observations":"Clear single-voice harmonic contours with gliding pitch at about 0.6-3.2 s, 3.5-4.5 s and 5-6 s. The lowest strong line sits near 700-800 Hz, with harmonics near 1.5 kHz and 2.3-3 kHz, so the voice appears to be pitched high. The contours bend and slide rather than staying level (rules out flat male vocals, A), there is one harmonic series rather than stacked parallel voices (rules out choir, C), and the pitch is too high and lacks the wide steady vibrato expected of an operatic tenor (rules out D). This points to high-pitched female vocals (B).","answer":"B"}
